In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever is guided by his guidance and follows his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: God, glorified and exalted, holds the whole matter in His hand, and to Him the whole matter returns; there is no reversing His decree; He is not questioned about what He does, and they are questioned. He is the One who says in the clear revelation: {They have not esteemed God with the esteem due to Him, when the whole earth shall be His handful on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens rolled up in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate} (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:67). And in His far-reaching wisdom He willed to seal the messages and the prophethoods with the sending of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and to make the religion he brought the completion of the religions; for God completed by him the religion for the people of the earth, so that no address can come to them from God after him. That is why He said at the end of the sending down of His rulings: {Today I have completed your religion for you and perfected My favour upon you and have approved Islam for you as a religion} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:3).

So God has approved this religion as a religion for the whole of humanity and has addressed it as such. It is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ that a rabbi of the Jews came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and said: Commander of the Believers, there is a verse in your Book which, had it been sent down upon us, the community of the Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival. He said: And which is it? He said: "Today I have completed your religion for you and perfected My favour upon you and have approved Islam for you as a religion." He said: Indeed I know where it was sent down and when it was sent down. It was sent down upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) while he was standing at Arafat on a Friday. And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) lived only ninety-two days after the sending down of this verse. That was on the ninth day of the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, so he lived twenty days of the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, and thirty days which are the month of Muharram, and thirty days which are the month of Safar, and died on the twelfth day of the month of Rabiʿ al-Awwal — of this month we are in. God sent down this verse upon him as an announcement that the revelation had come to an end, and that the religion God has approved for humanity is this Islam that was sent down upon Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him). So God undertook its preservation and its spread and its victory; and you know that He is able to fulfil what He undertakes, and that He does not break His promise.

His undertaking to preserve it has been evident in several manifestations. The first of them is the preservation of the Book that was sent down with it. The earlier Books — their own people were charged with preserving them, so the rabbis and the monks preserved them; but this Book God took upon Himself to preserve. That is why God said, in mentioning the Torah: {By it the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews, and the sages and the rabbis, by what they were entrusted to preserve of the Book of God, and they were witnesses over it} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:44); and said of the Qur'an: {Indeed We, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its preservers} (Sūrat al-Ḥijr 15:9); and said of it: {Falsehood does not come to it from before it or from behind it: a sending down from One All-Wise, All-Praiseworthy} (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:42); and said of it: {The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue; and indeed it is in the scriptures of the ancients} (Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:193–196). So God took upon Himself its preservation. This Qur'an, preserved in breasts, recited by tongues, written in the copies — as long as it exists on the earth, that is the continuance of this religion and its preservation. It is not possible for this religion to be assailed, nor for anything of it to be diminished, as long as this Qur'an stands in the earth as a proof against its people. God challenged by it the two weighty kinds, humankind and the jinn, to bring a chapter like it. Some of the foolish attempted that and arrived at no result. Musaylimah the liar came — and he was among the eloquent of Banu Hanifah — and tried to imitate any chapter of the Qur'an, and produced nothing but absurdities at which the intelligent are astonished. He heard Sūrat al-Fīl: {Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their scheming go astray? And He sent against them birds in flocks, pelting them with stones of baked clay, and made them like eaten-up straw} (Sūrat al-Fīl 105:1–5) — and it is the utmost in eloquence and concision. It contains a complete account of a great story of history, and mentions what is in it of lessons and signs, and sets out its effects and what followed from it. So he came — and God gave him power over himself — and produced nothing but his words: "The elephant, and what is the elephant, and what will make you know what the elephant is? Its tail is short and its trunk is long." There is no benefit in this; the intelligent only laugh at it. Likewise when he heard the words of God Most High: {By those that scatter, scattering; and those that carry a burden; and those that run with ease; and those that apportion a command} (Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt 51:1–4). For all that is in this chapter of great eloquence, among the greatest of it is what is in it of rhetorical artistry: "wa-l-dhāriyāti dharwan" — here the rhyme-vowel is a fatḥah, dharwan; "fa-l-ḥāmilāti wiqran" — the rhyme-vowel is a kasrah; "fa-l-jāriyāti yusran" — it is a ḍammah; following the order of the vowels, fatḥah then kasrah then ḍammah, in addition to what is in it of inimitability of wording. He tried to produce something to match this and said: "and those that grind, grinding, and those that knead, kneading" — and produced nothing.

Likewise, the later enemies of God Most High have been troubled by the existence of this Qur'an and its continuance. When the English government met, in times past, to carry out a plot against the Muslims, their speaker rose among them and carried a copy of the noble Qur'an and said: As long as this Book is in the hands of the Muslims, you will not attain your aim from them. So this Book remains the preserver of this religion, as a demonstration that the future belongs to it. If a Muslim finds himself in straits and the nations set upon him together, he will find relief in the Book of God. If he finds sickness and pain, he will find relief in the Book of God: {And We send down of the Qur'an what is a healing and a mercy for the believers} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:82). If he does not know a ruling, he will find the answer in the Book of God. If he does not know a moral quality, he will find the answer in the Book of God. In it is the solution of every problem. Therefore whoever has the Qur'an for a companion cannot feel estrangement, and whoever lives in the shade of the Qur'an cannot feel exposed. So this community must recall and keep before it this greatness with which God has honoured it by the remaining of the Book of God in its midst; and it is a consolation for everything that happens. Whenever a strait came, or the idolaters argued with a specious objection, there was sent down of the Qur'an what relieved that. Read, if you wish, the words of God Most High: {And a Qur'an We have divided, that you may recite it to people at intervals; and We have sent it down in successive revelations. Say: believe in it or do not believe. Indeed those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration and say: glory be to our Lord; the promise of our Lord is surely fulfilled. And they fall down upon their faces weeping} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:106–109). And read likewise His words, exalted is He: {And those who disbelieve say: why was the Qur'an not sent down upon him all at once? Thus — that We may make your heart firm by it; and We have recited it in careful arrangement. And they bring you no similitude but that We bring you the truth and a better exposition} (Sūrat al-Furqān 25:32–33). If people complain of one of the defeats, they take refuge in the Qur'an and find in it the stories of those who went before and what they suffered of harm and of straits, and find that their own condition will be made broad. If they read, in a time of straitness and hardship, the words of God Most High: {Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them, and whoever We willed was delivered; and Our might is not turned back from the criminal people. Indeed in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding. It is not a fabricated tale, but a confirmation of what came before it, and a detailed exposition of everything, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe} (Sūrat Yūsuf 12:110–111) — they know that what they are in is only one link in the chain of history, and one of God's customary trials by which He tests His servants; and that whenever hardship comes, with it are two eases: {Indeed with hardship comes ease; indeed with hardship comes ease} (Sūrat al-Sharḥ 94:5–6). And when straitness comes and there is patience, then victory is with patience; and when distress comes, then relief is with distress. By this a Muslim is strengthened with a strength that has no limits.

That is why, when one of the scholars was harassed by people and imprisoned and exiled and had his property confiscated, someone came to him while he was in prison and looked at his state, and found him in the utmost delight and happiness, and said: Abu al-ʿAbbas, what delights you? He said: What my enemies do to me. My killing is martyrdom, my exile a journey, and my imprisonment a retreat. My garden is in my breast; this Qur'an is in my hands. So whoever finds breadth in the Book of God cannot be straitened.

Likewise, among the manifestations of this religion's remaining and its continuance is that God, glorified and exalted, undertook to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that He would send to this community, at the head of every hundred years, someone to renew for it the affair of its religion. These renewers who renew the affair of the religion did not do so of their own accord, and were not sent by a state or an authority; rather the Sovereign, the Requiter, sent them to renew the affair of the religion, in fulfilment of His promise to His noble Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him). So they renew what people have come to be ignorant of in the affair of the religion. That is why al-Khatib al-Baghdadi brought out in Sharaf Aṣḥāb al-Ḥadīth, and Abu ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in the introduction to al-Tamhīd, from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: This knowledge will be carried by the upright of every generation, who will repel from it the distortion of the extremists, the false claims of the falsifiers, and the misinterpretation of the ignorant. Those are the ones God, glorified and exalted, fashioned and granted success, to make them trustees over His revelation; and God would not entrust His revelation to the bankrupt. He must choose for it the trustworthy, those who sign on behalf of the Lord of the worlds, whom God marks out by what He has given them and by what He has granted them success in and made them upright in, so that they may preserve the religion of God, glorified and exalted. You know that this Qur'an is kept far from filth and dirt and impurities, and that if it is in the house of one of you he will put it in the noblest place in the house and the purest and the cleanest of it; and that is by God's command. So likewise He cannot choose for it, of its vessels, any but the cleanest of people in heart, and the most God-fearing of them, and the most sincere towards Him and self-sacrificing in His path. Those are the ones who are made trustees over the Book of God.

Then this renewal which God has undertaken for this religion includes its renewal with regard to the new cases that arise; for novel cases and events arise anew and people search in them for the ruling of God, and God brings out for it someone who derives it and brings it out from the Qur'an or from the Sunnah and sets it out for people as though it had been sent down now. And likewise what they use to refute the specious objections of the slanderers and the innovations of the innovators, and what God supports them with of success in finding the evidences and setting them out. Among the aspects of renewal likewise is what they renew of the reviving of the spirit of hope in people, and of the reviving of self-sacrifice in them, and of alerting them to the dangers surrounding them. All of that is part of renewing the affair of the religion, because when the community feels that the religion is threatened, there is no doubt that it will exert its utmost effort in defending its religion, since it is the most precious thing it has.

Likewise, among the manifestations of this religion's continuance is that God, glorified and exalted, made this community the last of the communities, so that it is the greatest in number of the communities of the prophets. It is established from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that the communities were shown to him, and he would see a prophet alone, and a prophet with one man with him, and a prophet with two men with him, and a prophet with a group with him, and a prophet with a small band with him — until he saw a great multitude and supposed that they were his community; and it was said: This is Moses and his community; but look at the horizon. He said: So I looked, and behold, a great multitude had blocked the horizon. And it was said: These are your community, and with them are seventy thousand who will enter the Garden without reckoning and without punishment. And it is established from him (peace and blessings be upon him) likewise, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, that he said: There is no prophet whom God sent before me but that he was given something the like of which human beings believed upon — that is, he was given a miracle such that, had all human beings seen it, they would have believed. But what I was given was a revelation which God revealed to me; and I hope to be the one with the most followers among them on the Day of Resurrection. That is why he said: No house of tree or of clay will remain but that this religion will enter it — "of tree" meaning the houses built from trees, and "clay" meaning mud-brick, like huts and the like: that is, no house of mud-brick will remain but that this religion will enter it. And he likewise informed us that it will reach as far as night and day reach. Hence the call to prayer is now raised in all the regions of the earth: there is no city and no village anywhere in the world but that in it there is someone who testifies that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God — and that will increase and become general. This is the promise of God, who does not break His promise.

That is why He, exalted is He, has set out this promise in a number of the verses of His Book. He said, exalted is He, in the warning of Moses, peace be upon him: {Indeed the earth belongs to God; He causes whom He wills of His servants to inherit it, and the outcome belongs to the God-conscious} (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:128). And He said, exalted is He, in the warning of David: {And We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants. Indeed in this is a sufficient message for a worshipping people} (Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ 21:105–106). And He said, exalted is He: {And God will surely help those who help Him; indeed God is Strong, Mighty} — and before it He said: {Permission is given to those who are fought because they have been wronged; and indeed God is able to help them. Those who have been driven from their homes without right, only because they said: our Lord is God. And were it not for God's repelling of some people by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries and churches and synagogues and mosques in which the name of God is much mentioned. And God will surely help those who help Him; indeed God is Strong, Mighty. Those who, if We establish them in the earth, perform the prayer and pay the zakat and enjoin right and forbid wrong; and to God belongs the outcome of all affairs} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:39–41). And He said, exalted is He: {God has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the earth, as He made successors those before them; and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them; and that He will surely change their state, after their fear, to security. They worship Me, associating nothing with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that, those are the morally corrupt} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:55). And He said, exalted is He: {O you who believe, if you help God He will help you and make your feet firm} (Sūrat Muḥammad 47:7).

God set out His established way in the darkest and harshest of circumstances for the Muslims, on the day of the Confederates, when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and the believers with him were besieged in Medina. Quraysh and its allies came upon them from the west, and Ghatafan and its allies from the north, and the Jews and those with them from the east, so that they surrounded them on every side. And the bedouin around Medina came to lie in wait for misfortunes to befall it, wanting to attack its grazing livestock or its crops, and supposing that those within it would be snatched away from the land and that no remnant of them would remain. And the state of the Muslims grew so hard that it reached what God set out in the clear revelation when He said: {O you who believe, remember God's favour upon you when armies came upon you, and We sent against them a wind and armies you did not see; and God is ever Seeing of what you do. When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes turned aside and the hearts reached the throats, and you thought about God various thoughts — there the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:9–11). Then God's relief, mighty and majestic, came; and this relief was not expected except among the people of faith and God-consciousness. That is why God Most High said: {And God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they attained no good. And God sufficed the believers in the fighting; and God is ever Strong, Mighty. And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them from their strongholds, and cast terror into their hearts: a group you killed and a group you took captive. And He caused you to inherit their land and their dwellings and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:25–27) — all of that by the command of God, glorified and exalted, and His decree.

At that time the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was saying to his Companions: I have been given the keys of the earth, and I have been given the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar. And he said: You will surely open the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar, and they will be spent in the path of God. So the hypocrites would say: Muhammad promises you that the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar will be opened to you — and here you are today, not one of you able to go out to relieve himself. Yet not six years passed before the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar were opened and spent in the path of God. At that time the Muslims did not exceed one thousand five hundred fighters, and they were besieged in Medina with no outside reinforcement and with no striking weaponry. Not six years passed before the whole Arabian Peninsula entered the religion of God, and the Islamic armies went out conquering to Iraq and Syria, and the conquests followed one after another and the territory multiplied and the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar were opened and spent in the path of God. This swiftness in that earliest age is an announcement of the swiftness of victory in this age; for this age of ours is swifter, and what happens in it of the unexpected is greater. A few years ago, which of you expected what has happened today of the developments of this age? For example, I am now hearing the sound of a mobile telephone: who expected it to reach what it has now reached, a few years ago? No one dreamed of such a thing; but that happens between the kāf and the nūn — if God wills it, it comes about. Hence it is not to be thought strange that God's victory should come without our thinking about the means and without our wearying ourselves with planning. That victory will come without fail; but it has conditions which must be fulfilled, and these conditions it is very easy for the Islamic community to fulfil, for their fulfilment is not required of every individual, but is required of the victorious group and the saved band. These conditions God has set out in His words: {Those who, if We establish them in the earth, perform the prayer and pay the zakat and enjoin right and forbid wrong} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:41); and He said: {God has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:55). These, then, are the conditions, and they are easy and manageable; and if they are fulfilled, the promised victory must come.

Likewise, among the manifestations of this religion's continuance is what God has made the believers firm with of the accepted certainties which no one disputes — such as His words, exalted is He: {Say: do you await for us anything but one of the two best things? And we await for you that God will afflict you with a punishment from Himself or at our hands. So wait; we are waiting with you} (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:52). What do the unbelievers want from the Muslims? What do the enemies of God want? "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things?" Either the Muslims attain martyrdom in the path of God, or they attain victory and the defeat of the enemies. This is a wondrous strengthener for the hearts of the believers, and it requires of them that they not be defeated in any state. "Say: do you await for us anything but one of the two best things?" — either martyrdom in the path of God, which is the better and the more telling and the greater, or victory over the enemies, which comes next to it.

Likewise, among these strengtheners is that God, glorified and exalted, shows them of the signs in this universe what indicates the truth of His promises and the truth of His signs that lie hidden in His Book: {We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth} (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:53). So today we witness a great deal of the coming to faith of the unbelieving and dissolute, who enter the religion of God in crowds and return to this religion willingly and without compulsion. Some of them return to it because of a scientific discovery he has made, and then finds that it is present among the Muslims in their Book or in the Sunnah of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him); and those who become Muslims because of scientific inimitability are many in number. And we find others who become Muslims because of scenes and sights they have seen at the time of war with the Muslims. Many of the American soldiers became Muslims when they saw the bodies of the martyred fighters in Afghanistan remaining for weeks without changing, as though they were smiling: with no odour in them, and no change of colour, and no disorder in the body. And many of the Russian soldiers likewise became Muslims because of what they saw earlier of the support with which God supported the believers. Among the strange things of that is what they reported today, for they tell the Americans in their war on Afghanistan — they say: as long as you have not seen the camels, no harm will come to you. They said: What are the camels? They said: At night we used to see by radar camels advancing towards the camp; we would watch them by radar and by imaging, and when they entered the camp they exploded, and were like rockets or like bombs. I have seen in an American newspaper, concerning some of the American soldiers who took part in that war in Afghanistan, that at night they saw a gigantic camel advancing, and they recalled the Russians' advice and fired bullets at it, and it had no effect on it: every time they fired at it, it covered more distance towards them, until it reached the camp and exploded. And it is observed on the screens that it was a camel with no one with it and not loaded with anything. But this is of God's stratagem and His scheming.

And like that, a number of those who are present in these wars see the patience and the endurance in striving in the path of God, and become Muslims because of that. One of them became a Muslim in Pakistan and said that he would memorise the Qur'an and would not leave Pakistan until he had memorised it — because he saw the aircraft bombing the fighters in their trenches, and when they turned away having emptied their loads, a man of them would come out and put his finger in his ear and give the call to prayer; and before the call was completed the people would come out of the trenches and perform the prayer, and then return to their trenches before the aircraft came. This is among the things the unbelievers witness and bear witness to, and it becomes a cause of some of them becoming Muslims.

Likewise some of the signs in creation that do not relate to the victory of the religion but relate to the truth of what has come in the Qur'an: the becoming Muslim of a great number of doctors because of the healing of some patients given up as hopeless, through drinking Zamzam or through the recitation of the Qur'an, is evident and widespread. And likewise some of the remarkable things they see, which may be an ordinary matter for us but which God makes a cause of some of them becoming Muslims. I met an English young man in Birmingham who had become a Muslim and whose Islam was excellent, and I asked him: at whose hands? He said: I became a Muslim at the hands of a cat. He became a Muslim at the hands of a cat: he did not become a Muslim at the hands of any of the callers to Islam, nor because of a tape or a book; he became a Muslim at the hands of a cat. I asked him about that, and he mentioned that he had been a limousine-taxi driver, and that a man from East Asia — he does not know whether from Pakistan or from Bangladesh or elsewhere — hired him in the evening. The time of the sunset prayer came and he asked him to stop and to leave the meter running while he prayed the sunset prayer at one of the mosques. He said: The man went in to pray, and I was content, because I had been working since the morning and the meter was running, so there was no loss to me. I got out of the car to stretch, and there was a beautiful cat at the door of the mosque. I went to pet it and play with it, and it fled from me and went into the mosque; so I came back downcast and sorry, and had not reached the car before it came out again looking at me. So I went back to it, and it went into the mosque a second time and a third. Then I realised that it felt that something inside protected it, and that I would not dare approach it if it went in; so I followed it a little to see what was inside. And I looked, and behold, all those praying were in the state of bowing and all of them humble before God; and I looked, and behold, all the people were submitting to the Lord of the worlds in a single posture. And that was the cause of his becoming a Muslim.

And another, whose father was a fanatical, extremist Jew of the wealthy English — and he is a doctor, one of the famous doctors in London — and a Libyan doctor worked with him in the same hospital in which the Libyan worked. A quarrel occurred between them in the hospital, and this doctor said: there is no people among the peoples of the world dirtier or filthier than the Muslims. The Libyan doctor said to him: this is not true; the place of filth, the filthiest thing in a human being, is cleaner among the Muslims than your own face. How many times a day do you wash your face? He said: Three times; in the morning this is enough. He said: The Muslims clean themselves even at the places where impurity comes out; they wash them. And he mentioned to him ritual purity five times — that is, the times of the prayers — and mentioned ablution to him. He denied this, and said: Come with me and witness that at the great mosque of London. So he went out with him, and when the two of them came to the mosque of London at one of the prayers recited aloud — I think it was the night prayer — they stood before the prayer at the place of ablution, and behold, people were coming at intervals and performing ablution: the African came, and the Asian, and the English Muslim, and the Arab, all of them performing ablution in the same manner, washing each limb three times, while the doctors watched that. Then he entered the mosque and said to him: Wait for me here; the time of the prayer has come and you cannot enter the mosque; until I pray and come back to you. So he stood by the ablution place while people were still coming, performing ablution and entering. He said: I waited a little, and when the door opened a beautiful voice with a quiet melody came out to me; and I wanted to hear it close up, so I approached the door and put in only my face, and I heard the imam reciting a very quiet recitation, with the people behind him in an awesome silence, listening to him. I heard that for a while and then went out, and the matter did not greatly draw my attention, for I often hear songs and chants; this is an ordinary thing for me. So I stood in the place where my companion had left me. And when the people had completed the prayer and given the salutation, they began to come out in groups; and every time one of them passed me he looked at me with an astonished look and began to come up to me and ask me: What is the matter with you? — until a number of people had crowded around me saying: Your face is shining and radiant. And I denied that and did not think it true, until my companion came and said: What is on your face? I said: There is nothing on it. He said: Indeed there is; your face is shining like the moon. He said: So I denied that, and went up to the mirror and looked, and behold, on it were the remains of the light they had mentioned. He found that the part of him that had gone into the mosque had become like a piece of the moon; and that was the cause of his becoming a Muslim.

Now what happened to this man — many Muslims enter the mosque and this light does not come to them; but it was a sign with which God singled him out, like what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to his Companions concerning Muhallim ibn Jaththamah, who killed a man who was testifying that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God at the time of his becoming a Muslim. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: O God, do not forgive Muhallim. Then he died, and they buried him, and the earth cast him out; then they buried him a second time and the earth cast him out; then they buried him a third time and the earth cast him out, and they covered him with stones. And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The earth conceals one who is worse than he; but it is a sign. The earth conceals one who is worse than he — but this is a sign. Likewise this man whose face became white: many Muslims who are better than he does this not happen to; but it was a sign that was the cause of his becoming a Muslim.

And like that, an American doctor specialising in internal medicine, to whom there came a Moroccan woman afflicted with cancer at an advanced stage. He told her that there was no treatment at all for her and gave her some painkillers, and advised her to leave the hospital, because her staying in it was costly, and to go to her village and her home until she died. That was in a courteous manner, but the woman understood from him that there was no hope for her life and that she could not live. So she said to him with complete frankness: Tell me, how much of my life do you expect is left? She said: I am certain that I shall die, but only tell me how much of my life you expect is left. He said: About a month. So this woman went and asked her husband to take her to Mecca the Ennobled. He took her to the Sacred Mosque and she refused to leave it; she sat in it drinking Zamzam and reciting the Qur'an. When the period permitted by the visa had passed, she found that her hair had begun to grow back — and she had been taking the chemicals that remove the hair — and she found that her health had improved. Then after a period she found that she had recovered completely and no longer felt anything. So her husband took her back to the same American doctor; and when he saw her he almost fainted from the shock, and ordered urgent tests for her, and found that everything was sound, and he did not believe it. He asked her the reason, and she told him; and that was the cause of his becoming a Muslim.

And another likewise was treating psychological illnesses. Whenever someone afflicted with a psychological illness came to him he would look for something that would give that patient ease; and he found that sounds are among the most telling of influences. So he used to gather kinds of songs and tapes from the various peoples — even the voices of birds he would record — and would let the patients hear those tapes. Until he came upon a tape of the Qur'an, in the recitation of Shaykh Muhammad ʿAli al-Minshawi, from Sūrat al-Raʿd; and he found that it had a stronger effect on the patients than all the tapes. So he tried to survey what was in it and heard the words; and the voice is very ordinary, not like the beautiful voices of the singers. So he knew that the matter did not relate to the melody and the voice but related to the content of the words. So he searched for an exegesis of this chapter, until he reached the words of God Most High: "Truly, by the remembrance of God do hearts find rest" (Sūrat al-Raʿd 13:28). And he said: This is the point. And that was the cause of his becoming a Muslim. And the like of this is very frequent throughout the world.

Likewise, among these good tidings which entail the continuance of this religion is that the bitterest and most obdurate of the enemies of the religion today is the American army — the largest and strongest institution of enmity to Islam is the American army — and yet the American army has an institute for training imams, the imams of the mosques of the American army. And three years ago the American army printed a copy of the Qur'an and took a decision that it is to be considered a piece of weaponry: that is, that it is to be respected, and that it is not lawful for any soldier to do other than respect it with the utmost respect, like the respect due to a weapon — even if he is an unbeliever, it is like a piece of weaponry and must be respected.

Likewise, among these good tidings that indicate that the future belongs to this religion is the return of many of the disobedient among the Muslims to God, glorified and exalted. For today we witness the increase in the numbers of mosques and the increase in the numbers of those praying in them. Those of you who were in this city some time ago no doubt remember when the number of mosques in it was limited and small and few, and when the frequenters of that mosque were a small number of elderly shaykhs; and today, praise be to God, the numbers of mosques are of this size and their frequenters of this number, and many of them are young men in the prime of life. And like that is what has been among the women — they whom the people of dissolution often make much of and make into snares of Satan and means of temptation: those of the women who commit themselves and are guided and cover themselves are steadily increasing in number. And that is not confined to one segment or one class; rather it is widespread among the highest levels socially and economically. And likewise what has been of this in the lands of unbelief: the numbers of mosques now in Paris alone are roughly doubling every year — no year passes but that the number increases in it by about as much again — in addition to a strong turning towards them. Scarcely is a mosque built but that it is filled, and especially on Fridays; scarcely is a mosque built but that those praying fill it.

Likewise, many of those who were dissolute and morally corrupt and who plunged into kinds of dissolution and disobedience have today become among those who call to Islam and who have returned to it; indeed many of them have become prominent and famous callers to Islam. Today you hear a great number of the preachers and admonishers and reminders who were dissolute and whom God then guided — for example Shaykh Ahmad al-Qattan, whose tapes and lessons you hear, al-Qattan in Kuwait; and Shaykh Muhammad al-ʿAwadi; and Shaykh ʿAdil al-Kalbani; and Shaykh Muhammad ibn Saʿid al-Qahtani; and Saʿid ibn Misfir al-Qahtani likewise. And in various countries there are a great number of those who were among the dissolute and who have become leaders among the callers to Islam. You hear of Dr ʿAmr Khalid the Egyptian, who was from a milieu deeply immersed in extravagance in worldly matters and from the highest social classes in Egypt in point of wealth, and who was brought up very far from the religion of God and commitment to it; and today great numbers of people are guided at his hands. Last week he attended the Le Bourget conference in Paris — the conference of the Islamic union in France, the union of the Islamic organisations working in France — and more than a hundred thousand Muslims attended this conference, and he was among the most telling and influential of the lecturers in it. And so likewise a great number of those who frequent the mosques today in every city of the cities of the world had been dissolute and had transgressed and been tyrannical and had reached the summit of disobedience, and then God guided them, and they returned obedient and not unwilling, and turned to the religion anew.

One of the Algerian engineers told me — and he had been among those who transgressed before — he said: I knew nothing called prayer. One day I was returning from work at the time of the afternoon prayer, and there was my father, an elderly man whom I greeted only once a week, though we lived in one house — there he was in front of the house. I said: Where have you come from, father? He said: From the mosque. I said: What is the mosque? So he took me by the hand, and there was a mosque near the door of our house, but in a narrow alley and hidden at the side of the house. I said: What do you do in it? He said: I pray, I and the group that is in it. And behold, he prayed with nine elderly men. He said: So I said to him: If you and these old men die, this mosque will be demolished and no one will remember it. He said: No; rather those praying will reach the door of our house here. And the engineer said to me — his name is Muhammad Habib Allah al-Bashir — he said: By God, beside whom there is no god, we moved out of that house as an extension for the mosque. This house — they gave it to the mosque and it became an extension of that mosque. And this is evidence that the awakening has begun anew.

That is why some of the students of learning studying here in Mauritania who are sons of Algeria mention that their fathers were their enemies: they would forbid them the prayer and forbid them the recitation of the Qur'an and forbid them the litanies of remembrance, and if they found any book with them they would tear it up, and would try to have their livelihood come from wine and kinds of dissolution. And yet there have come out from among these people students of learning who have emigrated with their religion and who study it to this day in the Mauritanian schools.

And likewise I recall a young man who came to us years ago here in the school, from Morocco, and who is still here in Mauritania as I believe. He mentioned that his father had died and left him a wine shop, and that he used to sell wine in it — *he found his father earning by that gain* — he used to sell wine in it, and he had no pastime but gathering dirhams and dinars, gathering the dirham while occupied with that. He says: Until there came to me an elegant, clean young man, who used to sit with me and talk with me; and then he began to invite me to visit the mosque, and I visited a mosque with him. Then he invited me to the reading of the ḥizb — the reading of the ḥizb is a customary thing in Morocco: all the people of the mosque take the Qur'an and read a single ḥizb with a single melody. Then I began to keep to the times of the prayer, except for the dawn prayer. Then I was taken by surprise: this young man, my brother and friend, began to come to me at the time of dawn and wake me, and I would go with him to the mosque. After a time he discussed with me the matter of working in wine, and said: Would it not be better for you to turn this shop into a shop of another kind, more profitable and with more visitors and customers, and better? It was the first time I heard that wine is a foul gain. I was taken aback for a while by what he said, and then I knew that he had told me the truth and that he loved me. And that was the cause of his guidance and his commitment.

And I recall that some time ago I and one of my colleagues were in a hotel in Casablanca, and we got up at the time of dawn looking for the mosque; and when we came to the man in charge of reception at the hotel and asked him about the mosque, he said: Go to sleep, or I will bring you the police. Go to sleep; let people sleep. I came to that hotel again a few years later, and behold, in the market near it people were praying the dawn prayer: the people had overflowed from a mosque inside so that they had come to pray in the alleys of the market, in the same place. So conditions have changed, praise be to God.

And like that is what you witness in the Sahara, against whose people a base plot was mounted to take them out of the religion of God entirely. In this plot young boys were taken and carried off to Cuba and to the communist states, and were given wine to drink in their childhood and ate pork and were brought up on dissolution. And then, praise be to God, those men have today become students of learning and its teachers, and have become, praise be to God, among the bearers of this call and among those who call to God, glorified and exalted. And that was not due to effort expended, nor to work undertaken by the call to Islam or by its people; it was rather from God's granting of success and His guidance.

This is not to be thought strange, for the history of this community is full of this sort of thing. You know that when the Tatars entered Baghdad in the year five hundred and sixty-five of the Hijrah and slaughtered the caliph and seven hundred thousand with him on the bank of the river — and a Tatar woman would come upon a number of the men of the Muslims and say: Wait for me here until I bring a knife to slaughter you with; and they would wait for her until she came with a knife, and she would slaughter them one after another while they looked on, because of the feebleness that had crept into their souls. It was only a short period before Baghdad returned to its standing and the Muslims returned to it in full strength and the Tatars were defeated. That is why one of the poets says of it:

*Baghdad, mistress of a time of manifold turns, clothed by time in its circumstances; she grew grey, and youth returned to her, and she never ceased to be tender towards the singular among men; she has not forgotten the time of sons whom she was bereaved of, when the wind of annihilation blew violently upon them.*

And there is much that is parallel to this. When the ʿUbaydids settled in Cairo and killed the scholars of the people of the Sunnah — they slaughtered more than three hundred scholars of them — and wanted to do away with the Sunnah entirely, so that their claimant claimed that the Sunnah would never rise again in Egypt after that day: not many years passed before God took them away and the Sunnah's standing and strength returned to it. And there came Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi, who had been one of their servants, and became a leader of the people of the Sunnah, and attained that standing while he fasted one day and broke the fast the next and always stood a third of the night in prayer. He was a hadith transmitter, and one day a number of the students of hadith gathered around him and asked him to transmit to them the hadith whose chain is linked by smiling — a hadith famous on the tongues of the transmitters — and he transmitted it to them and did not smile. They said: If our master would permit himself a smile, so that the hadith may be linked for us. He said: I am ashamed before God to smile while Jerusalem is in the hands of the Crusaders. Then he campaigned against the Crusaders until he drove them out of Jerusalem and liberated it from them.

And likewise what happened to the Turks when they campaigned against the city of Heraclius, which is Constantinople, of which the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Constantinople, the city of Heraclius, will be opened to you; and excellent is the commander who is its commander, and excellent is the army which is its army. Muhammad the Conqueror went out to besiege it knowing that the kings of the Muslims and their princes had from ancient times campaigned against it for the sake of this promise, hoping to be among those promised by this promise: excellent is the commander who is its commander, and excellent is the army which is its army. Yazid ibn Muʿawiyah campaigned against it, and with him was Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and a great number of the Muslims' commanders campaigned against it and it was not opened. Then he campaigned against it and God opened it to him. And when it was opened, and he entered, mighty and victorious, the church of Hagia Sophia — which is the great mosque in Constantinople, in Istanbul now — and the Muslims gathered for the prayer, he said: Is there among the scholars of the Muslims in the army today anyone who, since he came of age, has never missed the dawn prayer in congregation, has never missed the opening allāhu akbar in the dawn prayer in congregation? They said: No. He said: It is a matter I had been keeping to my Lord's account and of which no one was informed; but I am compelled to make it known today: I have not missed the opening allāhu akbar in the dawn prayer in congregation since I came of age until this moment of mine. And he went forward and led the people in prayer.

Likewise, among these good tidings that indicate that the future belongs to this religion is that red communism, which disfigures peoples and deports them — and you know what happened under it before of despotism and harshness; you know that the people of Chechnya were subjected before to deportation and extermination and were driven out of their land entirely, the whole people deported from its land; and the neighbouring peoples likewise crouched under the authority of communism for seventy years — and today, here, there come out from among them the singular models who defend Islam, such as the commander Dzhokhar Dudayev, may God have mercy on him, and the commander Shamil Basayev, and others besides these among those who strive in the path of God.

And I recall, before the fall of communism, that we were on a visit there and met an elderly Russian Muslim woman, who said that if she were to find someone who would show her a copy of the Qur'an she would give him all her jewellery and her possessions — merely to see a copy of the Qur'an. She says: My soul longs to see a copy of the Qur'an — and she does not know how many parts it is. So I was about to give her a copy of the Qur'an, and my companions advised me: Do not do it, for if you did she would die on the spot, out of joy at it. And at that time, for all its harshness and severity, the young men were studying the rulings of ritual purity and the prayer and the acts of worship underground, in cellars; and therefore they are the ones who have come forth today, and they are the ones who lead the Muslims today in all the Islamic republics — those who used to learn the rulings under the authority of communism, which struck with an iron hand; they used to learn the matters of the religion in cellars underground. And I recall that young men from Tajikistan came to me wanting to study, and I found that each one of them wore clothes in which he had made hiding places for books, and that they buy copies of books that are very small and compressed and put them inside their clothes so that they cannot be discovered by any means, and bring them out with difficulty from inside their clothes and then put them back after the end of the lesson.

All of this is evidence that this religion is great, and that it will never retreat and never be defeated, and that the trials and afflictions that befall this community are only landmarks on the road of truth, and calamities that befell those who are better than we are; and the matter will continue to better than it was. There must remain in this community those who strive in the path of God and raise high the word of God and support the truth; and the traces are clear and bear witness to this, and only an obstinate man denies them.

For this reason a man of the Palestinians told me that he met a rabbi of the Jews in Palestine and said to him: What do you know about the coming battles? He said: What business is it of yours? He said: We hear that the Jews will be defeated in Palestine and that their state will fall. He said: Yes, that will happen; but you are not the ones who will do it. He said: And how do you know? He said: The ones who will do it are those whose number at the dawn prayer in the mosques is like their number at the Friday prayer. When the number that attends the dawn prayer in congregation reaches the number that attends the Friday prayer, then yes, that will happen. And what this Jew said, its features have begun to appear today. The man who told me this has died, may God have mercy on him; he was one of the shaykhs of Jerusalem, named Bayyud al-Tamimi, of the descendants of Tamim al-Dari, may God's mercy be upon him, and he was a member of the Fiqh Academy. And today a number of those who come from Palestine, from inside, tell me of a remarkable turning towards God, glorified and exalted, and especially among the young men and the women; and they mention such commitment among the people as no one can conceive, under Zionist repression and humiliations and harm.

That is why ʿAbd al-Fattah Mourou reported before — he was asked about the revival in Tunisia and about the Islamic awakening in it, what was its cause, given that Tunisia was earlier concentrated upon by the French in order to disfigure it culturally and completely, and that what they did not carry out Bourguiba carried out. He said: The beginning of the awakening in Tunisia was a drop of the blood of Sayyid Qutb. They said: How is that? He said: When Sayyid Qutb was killed, the news of his killing reached the Muslims in Tunisia, while the young men were sunk in their own affairs, knowing nothing of the reality of their community nor of the call to Islam nor of striving in the path of God. Then they thought about this matter, and the awakening in Tunisia began with three individuals who were studying the Mukhtaṣar of al-Akhdari, studying it together in the mosque. And with these three there began this widespread awakening by which people in Tunisia entered the religion of God in crowds. And this is among the strange wonders.

And like it is what happened in Libya long ago, when the Italian fascists thought that they had done away with the spirit of striving in Libya entirely, and found that the fighters were increasing in number — every period the number increased; every period the number increased, while the blockade continued and the killing and the displacement; and all of that only increased their numbers. So one of them said his famous words: The Muslim fighters are like the pine tree: every time a branch is cut from it, two branches grow. The number increases, and neither killing nor displacement nor prisons increase it except in increase and advance.

And who would have thought that Turkey, which Mustafa Kemal Atatürk disfigured, in which the call to prayer in Arabic was forbidden and in which the head-covering was forbidden, would return to its present state today? Whoever visits Turkey now, having visited it before, ten years ago or fifteen years ago, sees something astonishing over this period. A single school in Turkey in which vast numbers of young men memorise the Qur'an with a most remarkable memorisation, the like of which I have not seen: a young man memorises the Qur'an word by word backwards — the word and the one before it and the one before that, until he completes the Qur'an backwards; he memorises it backwards as he memorises it forwards, and he memorises it by the numbers of the verses and the numbers of the chapters: if you say to him, give me number such-and-such, such-and-such a verse of such-and-such a chapter, he sets off straight away. And this school stands to this day, and there are very many like it among the scholarly and Qur'anic schools; and people's turning to the head-covering and to commitment is a very great thing.

All of this shows us that the future belongs to this religion, and that every harassment of it cannot affect it and can only increase the turning towards it. That is why you know that the awakening in this country benefited greatly from what happened of the suppression of the awakening in Algeria: when people were suppressed in Algeria, people here became zealous for the religion, and many of the Mauritanian young men returned to commitment to the religion when they heard the news. And whenever an event like this occurs — if a problem occurs in Palestine and the Muslims there are harmed, or in Iraq, or in any place — Islam spreads in other parts. One man has likened it to the dry land of the earth: the dry part of the earth is about a quarter, and the rest of it is all seas; but if it were supposed that one of the islands were swallowed up and disappeared, the same measure of dry land would have to appear as well. If one of the continents disappeared, another continent would appear, because the matter is built upon this balance. And so, if harassment occurs on one side, extension and increase appear on another side. And this is nothing but the parallel of the poet's words:

*It is as though my eye and my heart, after you, were the two extremities of a luxuriant branch of the green ben-tree: water flows down one side of it while a blazing fire is kindled on the other side.*

Or as Abu Bakr ibn Durayd, may God have mercy on him, said:

*A heart cut to pieces, turned to blood, so that it flowed and streamed with the tears as tears; its sighs were sent back into its inward parts, and shattered ribs and sides from it. Wonder at a fire kindled in his breast that drew forth a spring from his eyelid: a flame that, when it burns in the entrails, is summer heat, and appears in the eyelids as spring.*

So whenever the harassment grows severe on one of the sides, the state grows broad on another side. God undertook to His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that He would not set over this community an enemy other than itself who would root out its whole body. If an enemy is set over one side, ease will come about on the opposite side; whenever hardship occurs in one place, know that expansion is occurring in another place. And this is a wondrous good tiding, because God, glorified and exalted, before this, when hardship came upon the believers in Mecca, the relief came by the emigration. The relief did not come at first in their original home in Mecca, but came in another place. They had at first been seeking a place of security, and emigrated to Abyssinia, and the place of security was not there but rather in the land of the two lava-fields, when it was shown to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): a land of lava-fields and palms between two mountains; and he supposed at first that it was al-Ahsaʾ and Hajar, and it turned out to be Medina.

The promise of God, glorified and exalted, is true and must be fulfilled. We ask God, glorified and exalted, to make us among those who support His religion, and to honour us by the religion, and to honour the religion by us. And may God bless and grant peace to our Prophet Muhammad and to his family and all his Companions.

flags.arabic: مثل القائد جوهر دودايف رحمه الله، والقائد شامل باساييف، وغير هؤلاء من المجاهدين في سبيل الله
flags.context: The passage on the peoples who lived under communism and the figures who have emerged from them.
options: Withhold this record from publication pending legal advice and a decision by the Sheikh's office
Publish with the passage and a prominent editorial and historical note
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED — HIGHEST PRIORITY IN THIS SLICE (house rule 12). The lecture names two Chechen commanders as 'singular models who defend Islam' and as among 'those who strive in the path of God', and prays for God's mercy on the first. Shamil Basayev is a designated terrorist in a number of jurisdictions, including ones in which Ummah Collective and its readers operate, and he was responsible for attacks on civilians after this lecture's subject period. Publishing this sentence in English, under the Sheikh's name and without context, carries legal as well as reputational exposure that does not exist for the Arabic original addressed to a Mauritanian audience in the 2000s. The sentence has been translated exactly as it stands: nothing has been softened, removed or qualified, because that is not the translator's decision. It is Ummah Collective's and the Sheikh's office's, and it should be taken with legal advice before anything ships.

flags.arabic: أسلم كثير من الجنود الأمريكان عندما رأوا جثث المجاهدين المستشهدين في أفغانستان … كنا بالليل نرى بالرادار إبلا أو جمالا تقدم إلى المعسكر … فإذا دخلت المعسكر تفجرت / أعدى أعداء الدين اليوم وأعتاهم الجيش الأمريكي / وقد شاهدت في جريدة أمريكية
flags.context: The section on signs that lead non-Muslims to Islam.
options: Publish with an editorial note marking the claims as reported, not verified
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED (house rule 12). This section contains a series of factual claims about a named living army and a named war — that the American army is the largest and strongest institution of enmity to Islam; that many American and Russian soldiers converted after seeing incorrupt bodies of fighters in Afghanistan; and the account of exploding camels observed on radar, which the Sheikh says he read in an American newspaper. The Sheikh presents these as reports ('what they reported', 'I have seen in an American newspaper'), and the English keeps that framing exactly rather than either asserting them or distancing the Sheikh from them. No source is given for any of them and none has been supplied. If the record is published, the site should make clear that these are reports the Sheikh relates, and should not present them as established.

flags.arabic: تعرفون أن التتار لما دخلوا بغداد في عام خمسمائة وخمس وستين من الهجرة وذبحوا الخليفة وسبعمائة ألف معه
flags.context: The historical example of Baghdad's recovery after the Mongol sack.
options: Translate the date as the source gives it and flag the error
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11 — never silently fix). The record gives the year of the Mongol entry into Baghdad as 565 AH. The event is 656 AH (1258 CE); 565 AH is a century before Hulagu was born. This is a transposition, almost certainly a slip of the tongue preserved by the transcript rather than a considered claim. It has been rendered exactly as it stands and not corrected. The casualty figure of seven hundred thousand is also as the source gives it; estimates in the historical literature vary enormously and none has been substituted.

flags.arabic: مثلا الشيخ أحمد القطان … والشيخ محمد العوضي، والشيخ عادل الكلباني، والشيخ محمد بن سعيد القحطاني، وسعيد بن مسفر القحطاني كذلك … تسمعون بالدكتور عمرو خالد المصري
flags.context: The passage on people who were dissolute and then became callers to Islam.
options: Withhold the named list pending the Sheikh's office and the named persons' position
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED (house rule 12). The Sheikh names six living, identifiable public figures as examples of people who 'were dissolute' (kānū fujjāran) before God guided them, and describes a seventh, ʿAmr Khalid, as brought up 'very far from the religion of God'. In Arabic, in a lecture about the mercy of guidance, this is praise; in English, attached to named living people and published on a website, it is a statement about their past moral conduct that they have not agreed to and that could be actionable. The names and the characterisation have been translated exactly and nothing has been dropped. The decision whether to publish the names belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: فإسلام عدد كبير من الأطباء بسبب شفاء بعض المرضى الميؤوس منهم بسبب شرب زمزم … جلست فيه تشرب زمزم وتقرأ القرآن … فبعد مدة وجدت أنها قد برئت تماما
flags.context: The account of the Moroccan woman with advanced cancer.
options: Publish with an explicit note that this is not medical advice
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED (house rule 12). The lecture relates, as fact, a complete remission of advanced cancer attributed to drinking Zamzam and reciting the Qur'an, and says that the conversion of many doctors has been caused by such healings. Presented in English on a public website, this can be read as a medical claim, with real potential to cause harm if a reader acts on it. It has been translated faithfully — the Sheikh is relating an account of God's power, not prescribing a treatment, and the English does not make it either stronger or weaker — but the site should not carry it without a clear statement that it is not medical advice.

flags.arabic: بتلاوة الشيخ محمد علي المنشاوي / قبل خس عشرة سنة / ويفحظه بأرقام الآيات / فلم يكن المطمأن هنالك / لو قدر أن جزيرة من الجزائر خسف بها
flags.context: Five points where the transcript is defective at the word level.
options: Preserve each in body_ar and render the evident sense in body_en
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). 'خس عشرة' is a missing letter for 'خمس عشرة' (fifteen); 'يفحظه' is a metathesis for 'يحفظه'; 'المطمأن' for 'المطمئن'. The reciter named as 'محمد علي المنشاوي' is almost certainly Muhammad Siddiq al-Minshawi, whose recitation is the famous one; the name has been rendered as the source gives it and not corrected. 'جزيرة من الجزائر' means 'one of the islands', not Algeria, and has been translated accordingly; the homonym is a real trap here, since Algeria is discussed a few lines later.

flags.arabic: «بغداد صاحبة الزمان صروفا** شتى ولابسة الزمان ظروفا** …» / «كأن عيني وقلبي بعدكم طرفا** …» / «قلب تقطع فاستحال نجيعا** …» / «ألفى أباه بذاك الكسب يكتسب»
flags.context: The four poetic quotations in the lecture.
options: Translate as prose and preserve the hemistich markers' information in the flag
flags.note: FORMATTING NOTE (style guide §4) AND SOURCE DEFECT. The CMS marks hemistich boundaries in these poems with a doubled asterisk and encloses them in guillemets; that markup is preserved in body_ar and does not appear in body_en. All four are given as prose in italics, as the style guide requires, and no rhymed English has been attempted. The half-line 'ألفى أباه بذاك الكسب يكتسب' is quoted without attribution and is a proverb for inheriting a trade from one's father; it is rendered literally.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.

This is a public lecture, evidently delivered in Mauritania in the month of Rabiʿ al-Awwal (the Sheikh says 'this month we are in' when giving the date of the Prophet's death). Its argument is that the future belongs to Islam, supported by God's undertaking to preserve the Qur'an, the promise of a renewer each century, the Qur'anic promises of succession in the earth, and a long series of contemporary and historical illustrations.

The source presents the whole lecture after the opening paragraph as a single undivided block of text. body_ar preserves that exactly. body_en has been divided into paragraphs for readability; no words have been added, removed or reordered in doing so.

Hadith attributions are kept exactly as the Sheikh gives them — 'it is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ', 'in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī', 'al-Khatib al-Baghdadi brought out in Sharaf Aṣḥāb al-Ḥadīth and Abu ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in the introduction to al-Tamhīd'. Where he gives no attribution — as with the hadith of the renewer each century, the hadith of Constantinople, and the reports about Muhallim ibn Jaththamah — none has been added, and no grading has been supplied anywhere.

The verses of Musaylimah's imitation of the Qur'an are translated as the doggerel they are, and are deliberately NOT set in the curly brackets reserved for Qur'anic quotation, so that a reader cannot mistake them for scripture. The Sheikh's technical remarks on the rhyme-vowels of Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt are kept in transliteration, since the point is the vowels themselves.

'المجاهدين' is rendered 'the fighters' or 'those who strive in the path of God' according to context, and 'الجهاد' as 'striving in the path of God' — not 'holy war'. This is the neutral rendering; it neither militarises nor sanitises the term, and the editorial flags identify the passages where the referent is a named modern conflict.

'العبيديون' is rendered 'the ʿUbaydids', the polemical Sunni name for the Fatimid dynasty, rather than 'the Fatimids'. Substituting the neutral dynastic name would erase the Sheikh's own choice of term; the point is recorded here rather than silently resolved.
